source_text: Nunc reliqua subnectam. ueniet igitur summi et maximi dei filius, ut uiuos ac mortuos iudicet, Sibylla testante atque dicente: , πάσης γὰρ γαίης τότε θνητῶν σύγχυσις ἔσται, αὐτὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ ὅταν ἐλθῃ βήματι κρῖναι ζώντων καὶ νεκύων ψυχὰς καὶ κόσμον ἅπαντα. uerum ille cum deleuerit iniustitiam iudiciumque maximum fecerit ac iustos qui a principio fuerunt ad uitam instaurauerit. mille annos inter homines uersabitur eosque iustissimo imperio reget. quod alia Sibylla uaticinans furensque proclamat: κλῦτε δέ μου, μέροπες, βασιλεὺς αἰώνιος ἄρχει. tum qui erunt in corporibus uiui, non morientur, sed per eosdem mille annos infinitam multitudinem generabunt et erit suboles eorum sancta et deo cara: qui autem ab inferis suscitabuntur, hi praeerunt uiuentibus uelut iudices. gentes uero non extinguentur omnino, sed quaedam relinquentur in uictoriam dei, ut triumphentur a iustis ac subiugentur perpetuae seruituti. sub idem tempus etiam princeps daemonum, qui est machinator omnium malorum, catenis uincietur et erit in custodia mille annis caelestis imperii, quo iustitia in orbe regnabit. ne quod malum aduersus populum dei moliatur. post cuius aduentum congregabuntur iusti ex omni terra peractoque iudicio ciuitas sancta constituetur in medio terrae, in qua ipse conditor deus cum iustis dominantibus commoretur. quam ciuitatem Sibylla designat, cum dicit: καὶ πόλιν, ἥν ἐπόθησε θεὸς, ταύτην ἐποίησεν λαμπροτέραν ἄστρων ἠδ\' ἡλίου ἠδὲ σελήνης. tunc auferentur a mundo tenebrae illae quibus obfundetur atque occaecabitur caelum, et luna claritudinem solis accipiet nec minuetur ulterius, sol autem septies tanto quam nunc est clarior fiet. terra uero aperiet fecunditatem suam et uberrimas fruges sua sponte generabit, rupes montium melle sudabunt, per riuos uina decurrent et flumina lacte inundabunt: mundus denique ipse gaudebit et omnis rerum natura laetabitur erepta et liberata dominio mali et impietatis et sceleris et erroris. non bestiae per hoc tempus sanguine alentur, non aues praeda, sed quieta et placida erunt omnia. leones et uituli ad praesepe simul stabunt, lupus ouem non rapiet, canis non uenabitur, accipitres et aquilae non nocebunt, infans cum serpentibus ludet. denique tum fient illa quae poetae aureis temporibus facta esse iam Saturno regnante dixerunt. quorum error hinc ortus est, quod prophetae futurorum pleraque sic proferunt et enuntiant quasi iam peracta. uisiones enim diuino spiritu offerebantur oculis eorum et uidebant illa in conspectu suo quasi fieri ac terminari. quae uaticinia eorum cum paulatim fama uulgasset, quoniam profani a sacramento ignorabant quatenus dicerentur, conpleta esse iam ueteribus saeculis illa omnia putauerunt, quae utique fieri conplerique non poterant homine regnante. cum uero deletis religionibus impiis et scelere compresso subiecta erit deo terra, cedet et ipse mari uector nec nautica pinus mutabit merces, omnis feret omnia tellus. non rastros patietur humus, non uinea falcem; robustus quoque iam tauris iuga soluet arator. tunc et molli paulatim flauescet campus arista incultisque rubens pendebit sentibus uua et durae quercus sudabunt roscida mella. nec uarios discet mentiri lana colores, ipse sed in pratis aries iam suaue rubenti- murice, iam croceo mutabit uellera luto, sponte sua sandyx pascentis uestiet agnos. ipsae lacte domum referent distenta capellae ubera nec magnos metuent armenta leones. quae poeta secundum Cymaeae Sibyllae carmina prolocutus est. Erythraea uero sic ait: οἱ δὲ λύκοι τε καὶ ἄρνες ἐν οὔρεσιν ἄμμιγ\' ἔδονται χόρτον παρδάλιες τ᾽ ἐρίφοις ἄμα βοσκήσονται· ἄρκτοι σὺν μόσχοισιν ὁμοῦ καὶ πᾶσι βροτοῖσιν σαρκοβόρος τε λέων φάγεται ἄχυρον παρὰ φάτνῃ, σὺν βρέφεσίν τε δράκοντες ἄμ\' ἀσπίσι κοιμήσονται. et alio loco de ubertate rerum: καὶ τότε δὴ χάρμην μεγάλην θεὸς ἀνδράσι δώσει. καὶ γὰρ γῆ καὶ δένδρα καὶ ἄσπετα θρέμματα γαίης δώσουσι καρπὸν τὸν ἀληθινὸν ἀνθρώποισιν οἴνου καὶ μέλιτος γλυκεροῦ λευκοῦ τε γάλακτος καὶ σίτου, ὅπερ ἐστὶ βροτοῖς κάλλιστον ἁπάντων. et alia eodem modo: εὐσεβέων δὲ μόνων ἁγία χθὼν πάντα τάδ᾽ οἴσει, νᾶμα μελισταγέης ἀπὸ πέτρης ἠδ᾽ ἀπὸ πηγῆς καὶ γάλα τ᾽ ἀμβροσίης ῥεύσει πάντεσσι δικαίοις. uiuent itaque homines tranquillissimam et copiosissimam uitam et regnabunt cum deo pariter, reges gentium uenient a finibus terrae cum donis ac muneribus, ut adorent et honorificent regem magnum, cuius nomen erit praeclarum ac uenerabile uniuersis nationibus quae sub caelo erunt et regibus qui dominabuntur in terra.
pass_a_gloss: Now I will add the remaining things. Therefore the Son of the highest and greatest God will come, so that He may judge the living and the dead, the Sibyl testifying and saying: For there will be a confusion of mortals of the whole earth, when the Almighty Himself comes to judge the souls of the living and the dead and the whole world. But when He has destroyed injustice and made the greatest judgment and restored the just, who were from the beginning, to life, He will live among men for a thousand years and will rule them with a most just command. Which another Sibyl, prophesying and raving, proclaims: Hear me, mortals, the Eternal King reigns. Then those who will be in bodies alive will not die, but through the same thousand years they will generate an infinite multitude and their offspring will be holy and dear to God: but those who will be raised from the underworld, these will preside over the living as if judges. The nations, indeed, will not be entirely extinguished, but some will be left for the victory of God, so that they may be triumphed over by the just and subjected to perpetual servitude. At the same time, the prince of demons, who is the contriver of all evils, will be bound with chains and will be in custody for a thousand years of the heavenly command, so that justice may reign in the world. Lest he may plot any evil against the people of God. After whose coming the just will be gathered from all the earth, and when the judgment has been completed, the holy city will be established in the middle of the earth, in which the Founder God Himself will dwell with the just ruling. Which city the Sibyl designates, when she says: And the city, which God desired, He made brighter than the stars and the sun and the moon. Then those darknesses will be taken away from the world, by which the heaven will be obscured, and the moon will receive the brightness of the sun and will not be diminished further, but the sun will become seven times brighter than it is now. The earth, indeed, will open its fertility and will generate most abundant fruits by itself, the rocks of the mountains will sweat honey, wine will flow through the streams, and the rivers will overflow with milk: the world itself, finally, will rejoice and all the nature of things will be glad, having been snatched away and liberated from the dominion of evil and impiety and crime and error. The beasts will not be nourished by blood during this time, the birds will not be nourished by prey, but all things will be quiet and peaceful. Lions and oxen will stand together at the manger, the wolf will not seize the sheep, the dog will not hunt, the hawks and eagles will not harm, the infant will play with serpents. Finally, then those things will happen which the poets said were done in the golden times when Saturn was reigning. The error of these arose from this, that the prophets of future things bring forth and declare many things as if they had already been done. For visions were offered to their eyes by the divine Spirit, and they saw those things in their sight as if they were happening and being completed. When the prophecies of these had been gradually spread by fame, since the profane were ignorant of the sacrament and did not know how they were spoken, they thought that all those things had already been fulfilled in ancient times, which, indeed, could not be fulfilled and completed while man was reigning. But when the impious religions have been destroyed and crime has been suppressed, the earth will be subject to God, and the sea will also yield, and the ship will not change its cargo, the earth will bring forth all things. The ground will not suffer the hoe, the vine will not suffer the sickle; the strong plowman will also release the yokes from the oxen. Then the field will gradually become golden with soft grain, and the vine, uncultivated and red, will hang with grapes, and the hard oaks will sweat dewy honey. The wool will not learn to lie about various colors, but the ram itself will change its fleece to a sweet red color, now to a saffron color, in the meadows, the feeding lambs will be clothed with their own sandyx. The she-goats themselves will bring back home their udders full of milk, and the flocks will not fear the great lions. Which the poet has spoken according to the songs of the Cumaean Sibyl. The Erythraean, indeed, says thus: The wolves and the lambs will eat grass together on the mountains, the leopards and the kids will graze together, the bears will be together with the calves, and all mortals, and the flesh-eating lion will eat hay near the manger, and the dragons will sleep together with the infants and the shields. And in another place, about the fertility of things: And then, indeed, God will give great joy to men. For the earth and the trees and the untamed animals of the earth will give true fruit to men, wine and sweet honey and white milk and wheat, which is the most beautiful of all things to mortals. And another in the same way: The holy earth of the pious alone will bring forth all these things, a stream of honey from the rock and from the spring, and the milk of ambrosia will flow to all the just. Men, therefore, will live a most tranquil and most abundant life, and they will reign with God equally, the kings of the nations will come from the ends of the earth with gifts and offerings, so that they may adore and honor the great King, whose name will be famous and venerable to all nations which are under heaven, and to the kings who will rule on earth.

pass_b_english: I now append the rest. The Son of the highest and greatest God will come to judge the living and the dead, as the Sibyl testifies and declares: there shall be a mingling of mortals across the whole earth when the Almighty Himself arrives to judge the souls of the living and the dead and the entire world. After He has destroyed injustice, executed the great judgment, and restored to life the just who existed from the beginning, He will dwell among men for a thousand years and govern them with the most just rule. Another Sibyl, prophesying in ecstatic frenzy, proclaims: "Listen to me, mortals; the Eternal King reigns." Then those who are alive in their bodies will not die; instead, throughout those same thousand years they will produce an innumerable multitude, and their offspring will be holy and dear to God. Those raised from the underworld, however, will preside over the living as judges. The nations will not be utterly exterminated; some will be spared for God's victory, so that the just may triumph over them and reduce them to perpetual servitude. At the same time the prince of demons, the author of all evils, will be bound in chains and held in custody for a thousand years of the heavenly reign, so that justice may rule on earth and he may plot no evil against God's people. After His coming the just will be gathered from every land, and when judgment is complete the holy city will be established in the middle of the earth, where the Founder God Himself will dwell with the just who reign. The Sibyl identifies this city when she says: "The city that God desired, He made brighter than the stars, the sun, and the moon." Then the darkness that veils the world and obscures heaven will be removed; the moon will receive the sun's brightness and wane no more, while the sun will become seven times brighter than it is now. The earth will unlock its fertility and yield most abundant crops of its own accord; mountain rocks will sweat honey, wine will run through the streams, and rivers will overflow with milk. The world itself will rejoice, and all nature will be glad, snatched free from the dominion of evil, impiety, crime, and error. During this time no beast will be nourished by blood, no bird by prey; all will be quiet and peaceful. Lions and calves will stand together at the manger; the wolf will not seize the sheep, the dog will not hunt, hawks and eagles will not harm, and an infant will play with serpents. At last those things will happen which the poets claimed occurred in the golden age under Saturn's reign. Their error arose because the prophets of future events set forth and declare most things as if already accomplished. Visions were presented to their eyes by the divine Spirit, and they saw those things in their sight as if happening and being completed. When these prophecies gradually spread by report, the profane, ignorant of the mystery and not knowing how they were spoken, supposed all those things had already been fulfilled in ancient ages—things which could not possibly be fulfilled while man was ruling. But when impious religions have been destroyed and wickedness suppressed, the earth will be subject to God; the sea also will yield, ships will not change their cargo, and the earth will produce all things. The soil will not endure the hoe, the vine will not endure the sickle; even the sturdy plowman will unyoke his oxen. Then the field will gradually turn golden with soft grain, the uncultivated vine will hang red with grapes, and hard oaks will sweat dewy honey. Wool will not learn to feign varied colors; the ram itself will change its fleece in the meadows, now to a sweet purple-red, now to saffron-yellow; lambs will be clothed with their own sandyx as they graze. She-goats will return home with udders distended with milk, and flocks will not fear great lions. The poet spoke these things following the songs of the Cumaean Sibyl. The Erythraean Sibyl says likewise: "Wolves and lambs will eat grass together on the mountains; leopards will graze with kids; bears will be together with calves and all mortals; the flesh-eating lion will eat straw beside the manger; dragons will sleep with infants and shields." In another place concerning the fertility of creation: "Then indeed God will give great joy to men. For earth, trees, and the untamed animals of the earth will yield true fruit to men: wine, sweet honey, white milk, and wheat—which is the fairest of all things for mortals." And another in the same strain: "The holy earth of the pious alone will bring forth all these things; a stream of honey-dripping water will flow from the rock and the spring, and the milk of ambrosia will flow to all the just." Men will therefore live a most tranquil and abundant life and reign with God as equals. Kings of the nations will come from the ends of the earth with gifts and offerings to adore and honor the great King, whose name will be famous and venerable to all nations under heaven and to the kings who rule on earth.
